title: PTSD pharmacotherapy beyond sertraline and paroxetine
bottleneck: Only two drugs (sertraline, paroxetine) are FDA-approved for PTSD, both with modest efficacy, and first-line trauma-focused psychotherapies leave up to half of patients symptomatic. Decades of candidates (NK-1 antagonists, AMPA modulators, prazosin) failed late-stage trials, often sunk by high placebo responses and patient heterogeneity.
why_it_blocks: PTSD is common, disabling, and biologically complex; a two-drug armamentarium from the 1990s is a standing indictment of psychiatric drug development for trauma.
current_state: Brexpiprazole was rejected by FDA despite early promise, underscoring regulatory hurdles. Ketamine, MDMA-assisted therapy, and neurosteroids are the leading investigational directions, with durability and safety questions unresolved. The pipeline's repeated late-stage failures have pushed investment toward psychedelics and neuromodulation, leaving conventional small-molecule development for PTSD nearly abandoned.
